title: Chess, But SCP-426 Makes Every Piece Think They're Toasters
summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with neutral SCP-426 ('I am a toaster') on a4. Each round it moves one square in a random orthogonal direction; every piece adjacent to it where it lands becomes a toaster - a useless immobile obstacle for the rest of the game. Toasters (and pawn walls) block the original toaster's movement, so it can be trapped. Narrator walls it off on the queenside, lets it toast an engine bishop and threaten the queen, and wins with a ladder mate.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
Neutral SCP-426 starts on a4; each round moves one square orthogonally in a random direction.

After it moves, every piece (either colour) adjacent (8 neighbours) to it becomes a toaster: immobile, cannot capture or defend, permanent obstacle that no piece can enter [inferred], belongs to no one.
Only the original SCP-426 moves; converted toasters never move.
SCP-426 cannot move through toasters; it can move onto a square holding a normal piece, capturing it ('the toaster could actually just move onto the knight, capturing the knight').
Kings: an adjacent king would be toasted [inferred; ends game].
